item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Aug. 16)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: Lala is a tropical storm again after lashing past Hawaii's Big Island
item.description: As a hurricane, Lala skirted past Hawaii's Big Island, where it brought heavy rain and the possibility of life-threatening flooding and mudslides.

item.title: How Lovina Zook left the Amish and found an online audience
item.description: This 23-year-old who grew up in a conservative Amish community and had never used a cell phone or computer is today an unlikely social media influencer, sharing stories and recipes of the Amish with her six million online followers.

item.title: Ex-Amish Lovina Zook finds an online audience
item.description: Twenty-three-year-old Lovina Hershberger Zook is an unlikely social media influencer: she grew up in a conservative Amish community and had never used a cell phone or computer or driven a car. But she left the faith, and her family, five years ago, and today shares stories and recipes of the Amish with her six million online followers. Faith Salie reports on a very un-traditional TikTok sensation.

item.title: Almanac: August 16
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: A summer of extremes: Weathering a hotter world
item.description: July was the hottest month ever in the Lower 48 States – another escalation of our world into a hotter, more dangerous planet, where extreme weather events – such as heat waves, wildfires and hurricanes – will become more common and more extreme.

item.title: A summer of extremes: Weathering a hotter world
item.description: July was the hottest month ever in the Lower 48 States, breaking a record last set during the Dust Bowl – just another step in the escalation of our world into a hotter, more dangerous planet. Correspondent Jonathan Vigliotti talks with climate journalist Jeff Goodell and atmospheric scientist Maria Molina about how changes in Earth's climate are increasing the likelihood that extreme weather events – such as heat waves, wildfires and hurricanes – will become more common and more extreme.

item.title: CBS News poll on whether Democrats split over socialism
item.description: Americans think more young people in office would make politics better.

item.title: CENTCOM chief visits USS Abraham Lincoln amid morale concerns
item.description: Meanwhile, Israel is being condemned by Lebanese leaders for strikes in the south that killed at least 11 people, including children.

item.title: 4 Renaissance paintings stolen from museum in Italy
item.description: Local officials have expressed their dismay and sadness at the theft which occurred during celebrations of the Virgin Mary.

item.title: Ukraine launches one of the largest aerial attacks on Russia yet
item.description: Footage shows a large column of smoke after Ukraine struck a major logistics hub in the Moscow region.

item.title: NATO fighter jet shoots down drone in Romania near border with Ukraine
item.description: It is the latest in a series of similar incidents involving drone incursions into NATO airspace from Ukraine

item.title: Ukraine's own ballistic missiles could strike Russia within months, says former minister
item.description: Mykhailo Fedorov, the former Ukrainian defense minister who is widely credited as the architect of the country's modern war-fighting strategy, told CBS News in an exclusive interview that he believes Ukraine is in a "technological war" with Russia.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: True crime. Real justice. To miss it would be a crime.

item.title: Police race to save murder evidence from being turned into scrap metal
item.description: Police say the driver of the minivan — who wore a mask, glasses and a hard hat — sprayed security cameras with blue paint to hide his crime inside an Oregon parking garage.

item.title: Security video helps lead to a masked killer who tried to hide the crime
item.description: Dr. Steven Milner, a well-respected Oregon veterinarian, was accused of stalking and disguising himself before murdering Kenny Fandrich — the husband of a former employee. Security cameras played a key role in how detectives pieced the case together.

item.title: Murder in the Parking Garage
item.description: A masked killer spray paints security cameras to hide his crime. "48 Hours" correspondent Natalie Morales reports.

item.title: Videos capture the moment a devastating 7.7 magnitude earthquake hits Indonesia
item.description: At least 47 people died Saturday after a powerful 7.7 magnitude earthquake struck eastern Indonesia, with authorities warning the death toll is likely to rise. Videos captured the devastating shocks and aftermath.

item.title: Mall reopening brings renewed hope to Palisades community after devastating wildfires
item.description: A luxury mall reopening is bringing renewed hope to the prosperous Pacific Palisades community in Los Angeles, California, after wildfires brought massive devastation last January. Mark Strassman has more.

item.title: Indiana requests federal aid as relentless flooding continues in Midwest
item.description: Indiana requested federal aid on Saturday as the floods that have devastated parts of the Midwest continue. Lana Zak reports.

item.title: Hawaii governor calls state of emergency as hurricane Lala expected to pummel Big Island
item.description: Hurricane Lala is now a Category 1 storm as it nears Hawaii's Big Island, bringing heavy rain, life-threatening flooding and mudslides as Gov. Josh Green calls a state of emergency. Andrew Kozak has more.

item.title: 8/15: CBS Weekend News
item.description: Hurricane Lala stalks Hawaii; Indiana requests aid as Midwest floods worsen.

item.title: Luigi Mangione pleads guilty in federal case, admits to shooting Brian Thompson
item.description: Luigi Mangione entered a guilty plea in his federal case at a court appearance in Manhattan Friday morning.

item.title: Air traffic controller saves day when 2 jets with same call number converge
item.description: An air traffic controller's quick thinking helped avert a dangerous situation when two jets, one landing in Phoenix and the other simultaneously taking off, shared the same flight number and radio frequency.

item.title: Justice Department expands military's power to detain migrants near border
item.description: The Justice Department issued a legal opinion giving the U.S. military broader powers to detain migrants near certain areas along the southern border.

item.title: FBI: Violent crime plummeted in 2025, murder rate hit 20-year low
item.description: The White House is touting a historic drop in violent crime as the FBI releases the latest data from its annual Uniform Crime Reporting Program.

item.title: Army temporarily grounds Apache helicopter training flights after deadly crash
item.description: The U.S. Army said Friday it is temporarily halting Apache helicopter training flights after two soldiers were killed earlier this week​ in a crash near Fort Hood, Texas.

item.title: Golfer Jessica Bang, 18, dies while preparing for tournament in Thailand
item.description: Jessica Bang collapsed on Aug. 1 as she was preparing in Thailand for a tournament and was transported to a hospital in Bangkok.

item.title: Walmart tomato soup kits recalled over Listeria risk, FDA says
item.description: The 14oz soup kits were distributed at Walmart stores in 29 states between June 30 and July 7, according to the FDA.

item.title: Flock CEO responds to abuses of its surveillance technology
item.description: The CEO of Flock Safety apologized for alleged abuses of its service by law enforcement officers as the company rolled out new changes to how it operates.
